about: The one list of what the platform shows and ships. hub.html and playground.html render it, with the products merged in from the apps catalogue's products.json (js/catalogue.js); test/js/catalogue.test.js fails if an entry claims a primitive its source never calls, if a link or image is missing, or if a page grows a hand-written card again. Paths in `source` are relative to static/. Apps whose code lives in the apps repo have no `source`, so their claims are checked there, not here.

learn.title: Learn the SDK
learn.lead: Seven demos, each the clearest example of one part of the SDK. Open one, then read its source.

templates.title: Build a game
templates.lead: Three games that are also templates: each is the reference for one multiplayer pattern. Read the source, then build yours on it.

products.title: Built on the SDK
products.lead: Finished apps, not demos. Each is a product in the apps catalogue.

entries.name: Chat
entries.imageAlt: The chat demo connected with two agents in the channel and three messages exchanged.
entries.blurb: The raw connection API: channels, presence and encrypted messages.
entries.text: The only demo on the raw connection API rather than the wrapper: connect by channel ID, resume a session after a reload, and approve another agent's key before they can join. "Ring me when I'm away" adds Knock: a content-free push that reaches somebody whose page is closed.

entries.name: Under the Hood
entries.imageAlt: Under the Hood with two people in a channel: relay mode p2p-host, who is here, a star diagram of how messages travel, and a log of what just happened.
entries.blurb: See who is connected and how messages travel between them.
entries.text: Presence, the elected host and the shape of the relay, drawn live. Press "step aside" and watch host migration happen — the part of the system every app depends on and none of them shows.
entries.call: onBecomeHost() { /* you are the relay now */ }

entries.name: Channel storage
entries.note: Its calls are now the Raw storage tab in Pulse.

entries.name: Pulse
entries.imageAlt: Pulse with two people in the room: a live poll at two votes, a question from the floor, and the version history each vote appended.
entries.blurb: Live polls and questions, with a history of every response.
entries.text: Live questions and polls for a room or a talk. Every vote appends a version rather than overwriting one, so the result has a history you can scrub back through. The Raw storage tab is the same calls with the poll taken away: put, add, read, list and delete on the room you are in.

entries.name: Whiteboard
entries.imageAlt: The Whiteboard with two people in the room and four thick strokes in black, red, green and blue beside the tool rail.
entries.blurb: Draw together and see every stroke appear across the room.
entries.text: A shared drawing surface — pen, shapes, text and sticky notes. Every stroke reaches the room as it is made, undo reaches everybody, and the board is still there when you come back — stored encrypted, so the server keeps a board it cannot read. Every save is a version, and History scrubs or plays back through them without touching the board.

entries.name: Evidence Chain
entries.imageAlt: Evidence Chain holding three site-inspection entries, each showing its content hash and the chain hash that covers the one before it — re-derived, and every hash holds.
entries.blurb: Attest: signed, ordered receipts you can verify offline.
entries.text: The demo of attest: the note goes to channel storage, its hash goes to the platform, which orders it, signs it and welds it to the record before. Alter an entry or delete one yourself — verification re-derives the chain and checks every signature without asking the platform whether the platform is honest, then names where it broke.

entries.name: Dead Drop
entries.note: Now the "Leave for later" mode of Drop.

entries.name: Drop
entries.imageAlt: Drop sending handover-notes.md straight to Dawit over a direct connection — 18 KB, sent, nothing stored.
entries.blurb: Send a file now, or leave one encrypted for later.
entries.text: Two ways to hand somebody a file. Send now streams it in chunks over the data channel, straight between browsers: nothing is uploaded and nothing is stored. Leave for later encrypts a note or file in your browser and stores it in the room, notes in channel storage and larger files in the Vault, for whoever opens the link next.

entries.name: Call
entries.imageAlt: A call between two people, Ana and Bo, each tile showing a live test-pattern camera, with the Camera, Microphone and Share screen buttons below.
entries.blurb: Camera, microphone and screen share, straight between browsers.
entries.text: The demo of WebRtcHelper's media side. The channel carries who is here and what they have switched on; camera and screen go peer to peer. Sharing your screen replaces your camera rather than adding a stream, and a camera switched off mid-negotiation never shows up late.

entries.name: Doorbell
entries.note: Knock is now "Ring me when I'm away" in Chat.

entries.name: Air Hockey
entries.imageAlt: Air Hockey mid-game with both mallets on the table, the puck in play and the two players on the leaderboard.
entries.blurb: Host-authoritative realtime physics for two to six players.
entries.text: Air hockey for two to six players with a real physics loop. The tightest latency test on the site — if the puck feels right, the transport is working.

entries.name: Gavel
entries.pattern: Host as referee, with a stored record
entries.imageAlt: Gavel with two people present and the bench opening a case: the charge, who is in the dock and a precedent to cite, beside an empty case-law list.
entries.blurb: A courtroom on anonymous testimony; the verdicts become case law.
entries.text: A courtroom run on anonymous testimony. The host is the only broadcaster and the referee; every player-to-host message is addressed rather than shouted, and each verdict is appended to channel storage as case law the next session inherits.

entries.name: Chess
entries.pattern: Turn-based, state restored from a peer
entries.imageAlt: A chess game between two players after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Bc5, White to move, with the move history and clocks beside the board.
entries.blurb: Turn-based play where a joiner is sent the whole game by a peer.
entries.text: Turn-based chess where the board is rebuilt from the other player, not from a server. A joiner is sent the position and the whole move list in one addressed message, so a spectator arrives mid-game with the history intact.
